feature.title: 終了済み公開対局の履歴取得
flow: The HTTP adapter validates the game ID and calls GameRecords::detail under the shared request limit.
The PostgreSQL reader reads public completed metadata and its entire bounded journal in one repeatable-read snapshot.
Typed metadata and contiguous public operations become a public DTO; corruption produces an error rather than partial history.

guarantees.statement: Anonymous detail returns public completed metadata and contiguous ordered public operations, excluding command receipts, retry identifiers and internal state.
Missing, ongoing and hidden games return not_found, while malformed IDs are rejected before storage.

History is accepted only after structural validation and at most 4096 operations. Corruption returns generic 500 without partial history, excess history returns 422, and storage unavailability returns 503.
Metadata and journal are read from one database view even if another connection changes both between reads.

contracts.statement: The detail handler validates the path ID, uses the shared permit and maps repository failures to generic no-store HTTP responses.

evidence.reason: An ID containing a decoded space returns 400 before the failing repository can return 500.
Fake corrupt, oversized and unavailable failures become 500/422/503 and fixed JSON with no-store.
Missing and ongoing real database records yield identical 404 status/body, and successful detail has no-store.

contracts.gap: The real-router fixture does not create a hidden record; its hidden behavior is supported by the repository test and shared error mapping. Shared admission and byte limits are mapped in public-record-search.

contracts.statement: DetailDto emits metadata and ordered action DTOs without internal request, receipt, check or outbox fields.

evidence.reason: The exact metadata key set, equality with list metadata and two ordered operations are asserted; serialized detail excludes each listed secret substring.

contracts.gap: This assertion covers one move and one resignation, not every move, drop and terminal-result encoding.

contracts.statement: Metadata requires distinct participants, a terminal sequence, valid storage scalar bounds and finish-count relations appropriate to moves or resignation.

evidence.reason: Direct constructors reject listed duplicate-player, zero-sequence and inconsistent move/resignation count cases.
Direct scalar conversion assertions reject values outside PostgreSQL signed-integer storage bounds.

evidence.reason: Repository lookup directly asserts a hidden completed record is not found.
Eight corruption mutations and excess history are rejected rather than returning partial detail.

limitations: No mapped test starts a player-server TCP listener. No guarantee is made that structurally readable history consists of legal shogi play.
Shared HTTP byte/admission bounds and reader role/timeouts are mapped in public-record-search and startup-schema-isolation.
Source links and successful test execution establish traceable evidence, not semantic proof or complete coverage of these guarantees.
